content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves a collision between the defender's combined answer and DR3's pressed chain for the Acts 2:30 loins/seed link, so K-C's chain-vs-chain method governs it.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"[CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"by footing: whether the judge must expressly itemize each chain's footing or may state the chain-comparison conclusion; I read the text as weighing the chains together, not verse by verse.","why":"The judge text treats both sides as chains and concludes neither forces the other, without relying on whether any single verse states the contrary in its own words."}
